paragraphs: Qodem lel arbaa asar tzarik lekabbed kol hachadarim vehabbattim shebbechatzer, vegam haishsha teayyen heteb bekol habbegadim bekisim shellahem ulay hinnichu bahem chametz, vaapillu al hassapeq tzerika libdoq velirot, veaz bitchillat lel arbaa asar bodeqim et hechametz leor hanner achar tzet hakkokabim tekep umiyyad, veyittol yadayv qodem shemmebarek al habbediqa vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: Before the night of the 14th of Nisan, all the rooms and houses in the courtyard are cleaned, and the woman also checks the pockets of the clothing well lest chametz was placed in them, and even where there is only a doubt one must check. At the start of the night of the 14th, immediately after the stars come out, one checks for chametz by candlelight. One washes hands before the blessing over the search.
takeaways: The house is cleaned and clothing pockets checked before the night of the 14th
The search takes place immediately after the stars come out, by candlelight, after washing hands

paragraphs: Tzarik libdoq leor ner echad shel shaava, velo yabi shenayim haggedelim o debuqim beyachad dehave kaabuqa, veen bodeqim leor haabuqa, vehannerot sheen bodeqin bahem natenu bahem simana chshsh" bealema shehu rashe tebot cheleb shemen shumman abuqa veayyen "moed lekol chay", vehannerot habbaim bazzeman hazzeh leirenu meare eroppa hem shel cheleb veen madliqin bahem:

clarification.explanation: One searches by the light of a single wax candle, and should not use two candles stuck together which are like a torch, since one does not search by torchlight. A mnemonic for candles not used for the search: Chashash-a (tallow, oil, fat, torch). The candles that arrive in the city from Europe are made of tallow and should not be lit for the search.
takeaways: Search by the light of a single wax candle, not a torch and not a tallow candle

paragraphs: Tzarik libdoq bachorin ubassedaqin ubekol maqom shemmaknisin bo chametz, velo yaqotz bibdiqato ap al gab sheyyesh lo tircha gedola shekkatele habbayit benuyim baabanim qetannim veen alehem ticha, ki mitzva zo hi gedola meod ulepum tzaara agra, veyibdoq bimqom qibbul heasuy bebinyan hakketalim sheqqorin bilshon arbi beshem rvvzy"n (adne challon ubelitot qir) vekayyotze bazeh, veim shakach o neenas velo badaq ballayla yibdoq bayyom tekep umiyyad achar tepillat shacharit, vetihyeh habbediqa leor hanner, veraq beaksadra sheorah rab en tzarik ner:

clarification.explanation: One searches in holes and cracks and every place where chametz is usually brought, and should not be lazy even though the effort is great, for this is a great mitzvah and the reward matches the exertion. One also searches in recesses and protrusions in the walls. One who forgot or was prevented and did not search at night should search during the day immediately after Shacharit by candlelight, and only in a very well-lit place is a candle unnecessary.
takeaways: Search every place where chametz is brought in, even with effort
Forgot at night - search during the day after Shacharit by candlelight

paragraphs: Lo yatchil shum melaka, velo yokal ad sheyyibdoq, uteima bealema leekol perot, o pachot mikkabbetza pat muttar qodem bediqa, vegam im yesh lo et qabua lilmod lo yilmod ad sheyyibdoq:

clarification.explanation: One should not begin any work and should not eat until searching. It is permitted to taste a little fruit, or less than an egg's volume of bread, before the search. Also one who has a fixed time for study should not study until he has searched.
takeaways: Work, eating, or study is not begun until the search is finished

paragraphs: Qodem bediqa yebarek "asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu al biur chametz", lepi shehabbediqa hi tzorek habbiur. veap al gab dimtzuvveh zo hi baa mizzeman lizman en mebarekim aleha shehecheyanu. mihu katebu haacharonim im nizdammen etzlo beged chadash o peri chadash yebarek shehecheyanu vikavven liptor gam mitzva zo. veim shakach velo berek al biur chametz yebarek kol zeman shello siyyem habbediqa. veim bodeqim immo bene habbayit yebarek hu lebaddo veyitkavvenu hu vehem latzet yede choba, velo yedabber ben habberaka litchillat habbediqa, veim dibber shello meinyan habbediqa tzarik lachazor ulebarek, vetob shello yedabber bidbarim acherim ad sheyyigmor kol habbediqa. veyatznia techilla hechametz sheyyesh lo, baabur akilato veyikpeh alayv keli:

clarification.explanation: Before the search one recites the blessing “concerning the removal of chametz,” since the search serves the purpose of removal, and one does not recite Shehecheyanu over it. If he happens to have a new garment or fruit he should recite Shehecheyanu and intend to also exempt this mitzvah. If he forgot to recite the blessing, he can recite it as long as he has not finished; and if the household members search with him, he alone recites the blessing and all intend to fulfill their obligation. One should not speak between the blessing and the start of the search, and if he spoke about something unrelated to the search he must repeat the blessing. He should first put away the chametz he leaves for his own eating and cover it with a vessel.
takeaways: One recites the blessing “concerning the removal of chametz” before the search
One must not speak between the blessing and the start of the search

paragraphs: Hamminhag shemmolikin im habbodeq qeara shennotenin betokah chatikat lechem vesakkin kede lechattet bah bachorin usedaqin, veyesh nohagin latet asara petite chametz bezuyot habbayit qodem bediqa kede sheyyimtzaem habbodeq vibaarem, upoh ayarenu bagdad nohagin lehannicha baqqeara hannizkeret meat melach, vehattaam dehassatan vegunda dileh mitqannein bemitzvat bediqat hechametz harbeh, velaken molikin im habbodeq melach lidchot hammastinim vehamqatregim, al derek sheameru bahasamat hammelach al hashshulchan, veod taam acher deosin ken lesimana taba shennizkeh leshanim rabbot libdoq bekol shana veshana, dehammelach hu siman leqiyyum diktib "berit melach" (bammidbar ych yt) shehu dabar hammitqayyem:

clarification.explanation: The custom is to carry along with the searcher a bowl with a piece of bread and a knife to poke into holes and cracks, and some place ten pieces of chametz in the corners of the house before the search so that the searcher will find and remove them. In Baghdad the custom is to place a little salt in the bowl, to repel the prosecutors who are envious of this mitzvah, and also as a good omen and sign of endurance like “a covenant of salt,” that we may merit to search for many years.
takeaways: Carrying a bowl with bread and a knife; the custom of placing ten pieces [of chametz]
In Baghdad a bit of salt is added as a good omen

paragraphs: Achar habbediqa ballayla miyyad yebattelennu veyomar "kol chamira veku' dela chizzattiha veku' libattel velehve keapra deara", vetzarik sheyyabin millat "chamira" shem hakkolel chametz useor, gam yabin dehabbittul hu sheosehu hepqer veen lo reshut bo, veyomar habbittul shelosha peamim kemo shekkatub b"machaziq beraka":

clarification.explanation: Immediately after the nighttime search one nullifies the chametz, saying “Kol chamira… d’la chazitei… l’vatel v’lehevei k’afra d’ar’a.” One must understand that the word “chamira” includes both chametz and se'or, and that the nullification renders the chametz ownerless, with no remaining rights over it. The nullification is recited three times.
takeaways: The chametz is nullified immediately after the search, and one understands the meaning of the words
The nullification is recited three times

paragraphs: Hechametz asur baakila beyom arbaa asar mearbaa shaot ulemala, abal bahanaa muttar beshaa chamishit gam ken, veellu hem shaot zemanniyyot, venachashob otam meammud hashshachar, veachar akilato yenaqqeh shinnayv bachatikat etz daqqa, sheyyaknisenna bachorin ubassedaqin shebbashshinnayim kede shello yishshaer chametz dabuq sham, veachar niqquy yirchotz veyadicha piv heteb bemayim vishapshep shinnayv beetzbao heteb dechametz bepesach bemashshehu, maaseh beechad shehaya nizhar harbeh bishmirat hammatztza belisha vaapiyya ubekol hilkot pesach, vehinneh belel pesach achar sheyyashan chalam deomer lo adam echad "oy lo sheakal chametz mashshehu", vayyiqatz veyitmarmer meod vayyebek beki gadol vechazar veyashan mittok bekiyyato, veyachlom vehinneh ish medabber immo veomer lo "zeh hechametz sheakalta hu shennishar ben hashshinnayim perur qatan chametz meakila sheakal beereb pesach babboqer, ubeet shehaya okel veloes hammatztza ballayla niprad oto perur mibben hashshinnayim venidbaq bammatztza vaakalo im hammatztza", al ken, kamma vekamma tzarik haadam lasum libbo dabar zeh lehizzaher beniqquy shinnayv heteb:

clarification.explanation: Chametz is forbidden to eat on the 14th from the start of the fifth hour (temporal hours from dawn), and it is permitted for benefit even in the fifth hour. After eating, one cleans the teeth well with a thin piece of wood and washes the mouth, since on Pesach chametz is forbidden even in the tiniest amount. A story is brought of a man who dreamed that he had eaten chametz from a crumb that remained between his teeth from before Pesach and became mixed into the matzah - to teach us how careful one must be to clean the teeth well.
takeaways: Chametz is forbidden to eat from the fifth hour of the 14th
Clean well between the teeth, since chametz is forbidden even in the tiniest amount

paragraphs: Mi sheyyesh lo chametz bachanuto vei epshar lepannoto mechanuto lemakero legoy shetztzarik lemakero beodo bachanut legoy, yizzaher lemakero kepi haddin sheyyeqabbel min hannakeri maot vayyomer lo beperush shehu moker lo kol hechametz peloni sheyyesh lo bachanuto, vegam hu moker kol hakkelim shemmunnach bahem hechametz, ki heki dela leheve kekelayv shel moker birshut loqeach dela qana, veyimsor lo kol hammaptechot shel hachanut vayyomer lo beperush shehu moser lo hammaptechot kede sheyyikkanes lachanut bekol et sheyyirtzeh veyaaseh bechametz shebbetoko kecheptzo uretzono keadam haoseh beshello beli shum mocheh shebbaolam mihu adip tepe shello yaaseh derek mekira ella derek mattana, sheyyitten bemattana gemura ushelomoh et hechametz veet hakkelim shemmunnach bahem lenakeri, veyimsor lo et hammaptechot shel hachanut kede sheyyelek hannakeri veyaaseh bechametz kecheptzo uretzono, mippene shedderek hammattana hi yoter nekona, dehammekira enam osim ketiqnah, vekol zeh yaaseh babboqer tekep achar tepillat shacharit kikdi shello yishkach mechamat tirda, veap al pi shezzeh haggoy machazir lo hakkol achar happesach veeno neheneh kelum, en bekak kelum kevan debeemet hannakeri qana kol zeh kepi haddin: veotam sheyyesh lahem mine metiqa sheyyesh bahem qemach lo yishhu otam babbayit, ella yimkeru legoy o yittenu otam lo bemattana gemura, veap al pi shehaggoy machazir otam lahem achar pesach, veken otam sheyyesh lahem dagan sheqqorin bureg'yal (chitta chaluta ugerusa), veken mashqeh sheqqorin "bira" tzerikin limkor lenakeri o leyittenem lo bemattana gemura veyiqqachem etzlo labbayit. veim shakechu velo mekarum o lo netanum bemattana lenakeri qodem pesach, veabar alehem happesach asurim bahanaa achar happesach. abal, sukkar habba meare innadya (hodu) veken qnd (gushe sukkar sheqop) habba meare eroppa veken matoq sheqqorin nibbet (gushe sukkar bidmut baqbuq) muttar lehashhotam babbayit bepesach veraq en okelim mehem bepesach. umi sheyyesh lo chametz bispina o beshayyara yimkerennu lenakeri bemaot ubishtar, veyabo etzel hammoreh lelammedenu nosach hashshetar ek hu:

clarification.explanation: One who has chametz in his store and cannot remove it should sell it to a non-Jew while it is still in the store: he should receive money from him, explicitly state that he is selling him all the chametz and the vessels containing it, and hand him all the keys so he may enter and do with the chametz as he wishes. It is preferable to do this by way of a complete gift rather than a sale. He should do this in the morning right after Shacharit lest he forget, and even though the non-Jew returns everything after Pesach - the acquisition is valid. Also sweets containing flour, burghul, and beer - he should sell or give them to the non-Jew, and if he forgot and Pesach passed over them, they are forbidden for benefit; but sugar from India and blocks of sugar from Europe are permitted to be kept in the house, only one does not eat from them during Pesach. And one who has chametz on a ship or in a caravan should sell it to a non-Jew with money and a document, and should come to his teacher to learn the text of the document.
takeaways: Chametz in a store is sold to a non-Jew as a complete gift, with the keys handed over
Chametz that Pesach passed over is forbidden for benefit; raw sugar is permitted to be kept

paragraphs: Achar sheggamar akilato beyom arbaa asar yisrop hu bikbodo ubeatzmo et chametz hannishar demitzva bo yoter mishshelucho, abal asur lizroq hechametz birshut harabbim mishshum bizzayon, vegam yesh bazeh chillul hashshem beene haggoyim, vehamminhag lesarepo bechatzer baaraba shel "hoshana", veayyen "chayyim lerosh" dap yb veachar serepato yebattelennu miyyad veyomar "dachaziteh udela chaziteh veku'", veyomar habbittul shelosha peamim, velo yebattelennu qodem serepa, kede leqayyem mitzvat serepa bechametz shello, veim lava kikkar qodem pesach, mutab lehachaziro qodem pesach veim lo hecheziro qodem yachazirennu achar pesach veen bazeh chashash, veim lo yachaziru yesh bazeh mishshum gezel:

clarification.explanation: After finishing eating on the 14th, he himself burns the remaining chametz, since there is more merit in doing it himself than through a messenger, and it is forbidden to throw chametz into the public domain because of the degradation and desecration of God's name. The custom is to burn it in the courtyard with a willow branch from Hoshana Rabbah. After the burning he nullifies it immediately, saying “d'chazitei ud'la chazitei” three times, and not before the burning, so as to fulfill the mitzvah of burning his own chametz. One who borrowed a loaf before Pesach should preferably return it before Pesach, and if not - afterward.
takeaways: He burns the chametz himself, and it is forbidden to throw it into the public domain
He nullifies it after the burning, three times

paragraphs: Hallobesh kuttonet chadasha mimmin habbegadim sheyyesh bahem chametz nvqsh sheqqorin bearbe nasa (amilan chitta), tzarik lekabbesah qodem pesach heteb heteb, sheyyishreh otah bammayim qodem kibbus kede sheyyukal lehaabir et zeh ha"nasa" mimmenna al yede kibbus vilabbeshenna bammoed, sheim tishshaer bazeh ha"nissa" shebbah az qarob haddabar sheyyabo zeh ha"nissa" betok piv bammoed bizman shehechametz asur bemashshehu, yaan ki darkan shel bene adam kekishchugarin miknasayim bebet hakkisse leechoz hakkuttonet beshinnehem, vegam lipamim meqanneach piv veken shinnayv bekuttanetto, veken yizzaharu lekabbes qodem hammoed mitpachot hachadashot baim meare eroppa sheggam ellu yesh bahem chametz nuqesha sheqqorim "nasa", veken yekabbesu hammappa shepporesin al hashshulchan sheokelin alayv sheyyesh bah "nasa", veken bebeged shepporesin al hammittot kesheyyoshebin alehem bisuddatam bashshulchan, sheyyizdammen chatikat lechem lacha o peri lach shennopel aleha veqolet min ha"nasa" hannizkar vetoem oto bepiv veken kayyotze bazeh:

clarification.explanation: One who wears a new shirt of fabric containing hard chametz (wheat starch called “nasha”) must launder it very well before Pesach and soak it in water beforehand to remove the starch - for if it remains, it may reach his mouth during the festival when chametz is forbidden even in the smallest amount, since people are in the habit of holding the shirt in their teeth or wiping their mouth with it. Likewise one should launder new handkerchiefs from Europe, tablecloths, and bedspreads used at meals, which also contain this starch.
takeaways: New garments containing wheat starch are laundered and soaked before Pesach
Care is taken with handkerchiefs and tablecloths that might touch food

paragraphs: Lo yishtammesh bekelim shel chametz bepesach beli heksher, ukepi tashmisho heksher shello sheim nishtammesh bo chametz beroteb berotechin, hekshero al yede hagala bemayim rotechin, velo yaknis hakkeli tok hammayim ella raq im hu roteach, veim nach meretichato yabir od esh veyartichu hammayim az yagil bahem, vetob lehashhot meat et hakkeli betok harotechin day sheyyikkanesu harotechin letok obi hakkeli ukede yetziat haggiul lachutz vekannizkar beshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman za"l, vedavqa shehaya muetet yishheh otam, abal lo yishheh harbeh, veqodem hahagala yesuppam heteb veyaabir mehem kol chaluda, veim yesh gummot shei epshar lenaqqot hachaludda mishsham tzarik libbun bimqom haggummot, vegam yedot hakkelim tzarik lehagil, veyizzaher lehagil qodem shaa chamishit kede shello yitztarek lekamma tenaim, vaapillu hammagil qodem shaa chamishit yizzaher shello yihyu hakkelim bene yoman, mishshum dela lachalop bikli shel issur, ki bishar yemot hashshana en lehagil keli shel issur ella im ken eno ben yomo, vehammagil al yede tzebat yegalgel hakkeli, vegam kissuy haqqeara tzarik hagala: vekatub beshaar taame hammatztzot parashat eqeb azhara merabbenu haari"y za"l: rauy lizzaher shello lelabben hakkelim shel nechoshet im bedil mehuttak kederek haolam lehishtammesh bahem matztza ad sheyyagilem techilla, lepi shezzeh hibdil shehuttak alayv naasa qelippa al hannechoshet umonea pelitat hechametz mittoko im yagiluhu achar kak, vehallibbun bibdil atzmo eno moil lepi shehallibbun natenu lo chaza"l shiur sheyyuttezu mimmennu nitzotzot, velibbun hibdil lo yitlabben shiur netizat netzutzot, velaken yoter tob lehagilo techilla liplot hechametz, veachar kak yilbenehu haggoy lepanayv bibdil, veyizzaher shello yikbeh hakkeli achar kak bemayim shellipne haumman shebbahem mekabbeh hakkelim shel chametz ad kan debarayv yeuyyan sham, upoh ayarenu y" lo nahagu bekak ella melabbenim kelim shemmishtammeshim bahem bechammin kol hashshana bibdil techilla, veachar kak magilim otam lehishtammesh bahem bepesach, veen anachnu mochin bahem, mippene depoh irenu en darkam lebashshel bekelim ellu bishar yemot hashshana chametz gamur beayin ketabshil sheyyesh bo pat veqemach, veraq bemachabat darkam letaggen bah issa miqqemach, vaapillu haki en zeh rob tashmishah, velaken en anachnu mochim bahem laasot al pi azharat rabbenu haari"y za"l hannizkeret, ak vadday yere shamayim tzarik lehizzaher bekak, veken bikli shenneesar mishshum basar bechalab, veken shear kele issur sherotzeh lelabbeno bibdil ulehagilo, shetztzarik lizzaher kol adam bazeh lehagilo techilla veachar kak yelabbeno bibdil, kemo azharat rabbenu haari"y za"l hannizkeret:

clarification.explanation: One must not use chametz vessels on Pesach without kashering, and the kashering depends on the vessel's use: a vessel in which chametz was cooked in boiling liquid is kashered by hag'alah in actually boiling water. One must clean it well and remove rust before the hag'alah, and where there are pits that cannot be cleaned of rust, libun is required there. Handles and lids also require hag'alah, [performed] before the fifth hour and while the vessels are not “of the day.” The Ari, of blessed memory, further warned not to whiten copper vessels with tin before hag'alah, since the tin forms a barrier preventing the expulsion of the chametz - rather one should first give hag'alah and only afterward have it whitened with tin. The Ben Ish Chai notes that in Baghdad the practice was not to be exacting about this order, but rather to whiten with tin first and only afterward perform hag'alah, and we do not protest against those who follow this practice; but a God-fearing person should be careful to follow the words of the Ari, of blessed memory - to give hag'alah first and whiten afterward - and the same law applies to any forbidden vessel, such as one forbidden due to meat and milk, that one wishes to whiten with tin.
takeaways: Chametz vessels are kashered according to their use; those used with boiling liquid - by hag'alah
Hag'alah is done before the fifth hour, after cleaning off rust

Hag'alah should be done first, and only afterward should the vessel be whitened with tin, per the words of the Ari, of blessed memory - even though in Baghdad the practice was in fact to be lenient and not particular about this

paragraphs: Nahagu lishtop hakkelim betzonen achar hagala, kede shello yibla hakkeli min likluk mayim rotechin sheal gabbayv, ki pelitat hakkeli nitareb berotechin, veap al pi shennitbattel beshishshim ap al pi ken nahagu lekattechilla lehaabiro al yede shetipa betzonen vekannizkar beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l, v"lebush" katab taam acher bazeh:

clarification.explanation: The custom is to rinse the vessels in cold water after hag'alah, so that the vessel not absorb the residue in the boiling water into which the chametz expelled by the vessel became mixed. And even though that expelled matter has become nullified in sixty parts, nonetheless the preferred practice is to remove this by rinsing in cold water.
takeaways: Rinse in cold water immediately after hag'alah

paragraphs: Kelim shennishtammeshu bahem al yede haur beyobesh, kegon shappudim veaskelaot sheqqorin bearbe "sg't" (reshatot veshappude matteket letzali) shennishtammeshu bahem chametz, tzarik libbun lehakshiram lepesach, vela mehanne lehu hagala, vehammachabat shemmetaggenim bah day behagala, abal morenu rabbi mosheh za"l katab tzerika libbun vehammachmir lelabbenah tabo alayv beraka, mihu en tzarik libbun rab sheyyihyu nitzotzot nittazin mimmenna, ella day belibbun sheyyihyeh haqqash nisrap aleha mibbachutz, ukele cheres apillu otam hamtzuppin sheqqorin "pirpure" (betzippuy operet) shemmishtammesh bahem roteach dikli sheni, lo yoil lahem shum heksher, ella yinnaqem heteb veyatzniem bemaqom sagur, kede shello yiteh lehishtammesh bahem bepesach, uqearot shehem kele mattakot seh metzuppim behittuk zekukit en lehagilam, vekol kele hazzekukit shennishtammesh bahem betzonen, apillu shennishtammesh bahem mashqeh heasuy misseorim shehu hanniqra "bira", yesh lahem hetter lehishtammesh bahem bepesach al yede eruy sheyyemalleem mayim veyishshaaru bahem k"d shaot, veachar k"d shaot yishpekem veyachazor vimalleem mayim chadashim veyihyu gam ken bahem k"d shaot, veyishpekem veyachazor vimalleem od mayim chadashim sheyyihyu bahem k"d shaot, ubazeh muttarim lehishtammesh bepesach, mippene shebbeliatam battechilla hayeta betzonen:

clarification.explanation: Vessels used with fire in a dry manner, such as spits and roasting grates that had chametz in them, require libun to kasher them, and hag'alah does not help for them. A frying pan used for frying is sufficient with hag'alah, though some are stringent to give it libun as well. Earthenware vessels, even coated ones, that were used with boiling liquid have no kashering available; rather, one should clean and put them away in a closed place lest he mistakenly use them. Glass vessels used with cold liquid (even beer) are permitted on Pesach by way of “eiruy” - filling them with water three times, twenty-four hours each time, since their absorption was originally with a cold liquid.
takeaways: Spits and roasting grates - libun; a frying pan - hag'alah
Earthenware vessels have no kashering available; glass vessels - filling with water three times

paragraphs: Bishar yemot hashshana im loqeach keli mattakot yashan mehaggoy tzarik lehagilo techilla, veachar kak yatbilennu, vibarek "al tebilat kele", veim hem shene kelim o yoter yebarek "al tebilat kelim" ken hamminhag poh irenu y", udelo keman deamar dibarek "al tebilat kelim" apillu im matbil keli echad, vehakkelim shemmaknisim bahem yayin o shekar leqiyyum sheqqorin bearbe "qrryb" (mikele zekukit gedolim) dinam kikle mattakot, veim qana chadashim yatbil otam vibarek kisbarat harab "bet david" za"l, udelo keharab "matteh yeuddeh" za"l ken hiskim ateret rashe harab haggaon mor zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim zlh"h veken hinhig poh irenu bagdad mishshanim qadmoniyyot, veken haya doresh barabbim bekol shabbat haggadol, veken haya doresh ateret rashe harab mor abi zlh"h bekol shabbat haggadol, veken ani haebed doresh bekol shabbat haggadol beezrat hashshem yitbarak, nimtza hamminhag bazeh barur veyatztzib veen kan chashash sapeq bibrakot lehaqel:

clarification.explanation: During the rest of the year, one who buys an old metal vessel from a non-Jew must first give it hag'alah and then immerse it in a mikveh, reciting “concerning the immersion of a vessel” - or “vessels” if there are two or more - such is the custom here in our city. Large glass containers used to store wine or beer have the same law as metal vessels. If he bought new ones, he immerses them and recites the blessing, and this is the clear, long-established custom in Baghdad, with no doubtful concern regarding the blessings.
takeaways: A metal vessel from a non-Jew - give hag'alah and then immerse with a blessing
Glass storage vessels have the same law as metal vessels for immersion

paragraphs: En lashin ella bemayim shellanu, veshoabim otam samuk leben hashshemashot, o ben hashshemashot, vekatab harab haggaon harab chayyim palagi'y za"l b"chayyim lerosh": zeman hammugbal lishiba hu asara deqim qodem qeriat ha"magreb" (haereb), beopen dekevan shennaasa shettem esreh shaot bishlemut veqara "hammagreb", az tekep umiyyad yapsiq millishob od. yeuyyan sham, veasur lishob lekattechilla lematztzat mitzva al yede goy veyizzaher lirchotz yadayv qodem sheyyishob veyomar bepiv "hareni shoeb mayim leshem matztzat mitzva":

clarification.explanation: One should knead matzot only with “our water” (rested water), drawn close to sunset or during twilight. The time for drawing is about ten minutes before the call to evening prayer, and once twelve hours have fully passed and the call to prayer has sounded, one must stop drawing. It is forbidden as a preferred practice to draw water for matzat mitzvah through a non-Jew, and one washes hands before drawing and says, “Behold, I am drawing water for the sake of matzat mitzvah.”
takeaways: “Our water” is drawn close to sunset, not through a non-Jew
Hands are washed and a declaration is made that the drawing is for the sake of matzat mitzvah

paragraphs: Tob shello tigga ishsha nidda bemayim sheshshoabin lematztzat mitzva ukemo shekkatab b"chayyim lerosh", veyizzaharu lekassot pi hakkad yapeh shello yippol dabar letoko, veim mannicham ballayla baggag yizzaher lehoridam qodem hanetz hachamma, shemma yishkachem vetizrach alehem hashshemesh, o shemma yihyeh yom meunnan deyoma deeba kulleh shimsha, veim yesh lo aksadra tob lehannicham ballayla baaksadra:

clarification.explanation: It is good that a niddah not touch the water drawn for matzat mitzvah. One should cover the mouth of the jug well so that nothing falls in. If the water is left overnight on the roof, one should bring it down before sunrise lest he forget and the sun shine on it, or the day turn out sunny [despite appearing cloudy]. If he has a veranda, it is good to leave the water there at night.
takeaways: The water is covered and brought down from the roof before sunrise

paragraphs: Hen lematztzat mitzva hen lishar matztzot tzarik lehizzaher shello yilloshu qodem ammud hashshachar, yaan shetztzarik lehamtin al hammayim shiur layla achat al kol panim veachar kak yilloshu bahem, ubeereb pesach im mukrach lalush qodem alot hashshachar mechamat haribbuy, tzarik sheyyishob et hammayim ben hashshemashot shel lel shelosha asar, abal im sheibbam beben hashshemashot shel lel arbaa asar en lalush beellu hammayim qodem ammud hashshachar detzarik al kekol panim layla achat, ap al pi deyesh maqpidim lehatzrik shettem esreh shaot meet hashsheiba, hinneh bishat haddechaq uletzorek gadol yesh lismok al otam disbira lehu desaggi belayla achat apillu en bah shettem esreh shaot, vetzarik lehazhir keshemmotzi mayim min hechabit litten lalush bahem shello yaknis yadayv betok hammayim, ki hayyadayim chammin hem umechammemin et haissa ukemo shekkatab rabbenu zalman za"l beshulchan aruk, gam tzarik lehizzaher shello yalush haqqemach achar hattechina ella ad sheyyaabor alayv k"d shaot, mishshum demartach al yede hattechina:

clarification.explanation: For both matzat mitzvah and other matzot, one must not knead before dawn, since the water must rest a full night beforehand. On the eve of Pesach, if forced to knead before dawn due to large quantities, the water must be drawn during twilight of the night of the thirteenth. As a preferred practice some require a full twelve hours from the time of drawing until kneading, but in a case of pressing and great need one may rely on those who hold that one night suffices, even without twelve hours. One must not put his hands into the water, since the hands are warm and heat the dough; and one must not knead flour until twenty-four hours have passed since grinding, since grinding heats it.
takeaways: Kneading is done only after the water has rested a full night
As a preferred practice a full twelve hours from the time of drawing is required, but in pressing need one may rely on one night alone being sufficient
Hands are not put into the water; flour is not kneaded within twenty-four hours of grinding

paragraphs: En lashin lepesach issa gedola yoter min tq"k (520) drh"m, veyoter tob lalush otah pachot min tq"k (520), veshiur issa shechayyebet bechalla hu qemach mishqal sheba meot veshiba veshibim drh"m, ki ken oleh m"g betzim vechomesh betza lemishqal habbetza y"ch drh"m, vekannizkar bapposeqim veayyen "chayyim lerosh" dap q"y yeuyyan sham, umeachar sheanachnu nizharim shello yihyeh beissa shellashin letzorek happesach shiur hachayyab bechalla, laken tob lehannicha kol hammatztzot achar apiyya besal echad vehassal metzarepam lechalla, veaz maprish challa umebarek, veim en lo sal o teba achat letzarepam, betokah, yannicha hammatztzot bemaqom echad veyipros alehem mappa shello yitgalleh mehammatztzot kelal veyaprish challa, vehabberaka shel hachalla hi "asher qiddeshanu bemitzotayv vetzivvanu lehaprish challa teruma", veap al pi deyesh mi shekkatab hannussach hu "teruma challa", hamminhag poh irenu lebarek "challa teruma", veken hayu doreshim ateret rashe harab mori zeqeni zlh"h, vaateret rashe harab mor abi zlh"h betzibbur bekol shabbat haggadol, veshamati shekken hamminhag beir haqqodesh tvb"b:

clarification.explanation: One should not knead a batch for Pesach larger than 520 dirhams, and it is better to keep it below that, so that it does not reach the measure obligated in challah (777 dirhams of flour). Since we are careful that the dough not reach the measure for challah, it is good to place all the matzot after baking into one basket, which combines them for challah, and then separate and bless. If there is no basket, one places them together and spreads a cloth over them so none are exposed, and separates. The text of the blessing in Baghdad is “to separate challah, terumah.”
takeaways: A batch smaller than 520 dirhams so it does not become obligated in challah
The matzot are combined in a basket or under a cloth and challah is separated with a blessing

paragraphs: Im shakach velo hiprish challa qodem yom tob, venizkar beyom tob en maprishin challa beyom tob kemo shekkatub beshulchan aruk siman tq"v, ketzad yaaseh? yokal belo challa, vishayyer matztza achat ad motzae yom tob veyaprish challa meotah matztza, dechallat chutza laaretz okel veachar kak maprish, veap al pi sheyyesh omerim dela amerinan bechutza laaretz okel veachar kak maprish ella davqa beheka dahava behu shiur challa beodah issa, abal im lo haya baissa shiur challa, ella achar kak tzerepam bikli echad venitchayyebu bechalla la mehanne bah leshayyer matztza achat lehaprish mimmenna challa bemotzae yom tob, ella tzarik sheyyeshayyer meat mikkol matztza umatztza kede litrom min hammuqqap, hinneh heeleti besipri haqqatan "mqbtzyl" haiqqar kisbarat hacholeqin disbira lehu gam bikhay gavna dela haya shiur baissa techilla, ella sheachar apiyya netanam bikli letzarepam, mehanne leekol mehem qodem haprashat chala, veraq achar kak yashir matztza achat veyaprish mimmenna challa, al ken im shakach velo hiprish qodem yom tob yismok al sebara zo leekol ulehaprish achar kak mimmatztza achat veayyen beshulchan aruk lerabbenu zalman za"l hilkot pesach siman tn"z seip y' vy" yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: If one forgot to separate challah before Yom Tov and remembered on the day itself - challah is not separated on Yom Tov. What should he do? He should eat without challah, set aside one matzah until the end of Yom Tov, and separate challah from it, since [for] challah outside the Land one eats first and separates afterward. And although there are those who disagree when the dough did not have the measure for challah in itself but only after being combined afterward in a vessel, here he ruled to rely on the lenient opinion, to eat and separate afterward from one matzah.
takeaways: Forgot to separate challah - one eats, sets aside a matzah, and separates at the end of Yom Tov

paragraphs: Achar sheyyebarek veyaprish yomar bepiv hare zo challa, kede sheyyiqra lah shem bepiv achar habberaka, v"g deikka rabbim disbira lehu dela baenan liqro lah shem, im kol zeh kevan deikka rabbevata disbira lehu haki, may hepsed yesh baamirat g' tebot ellu lemebad allibba dekulle alema, ken heeleti bs"d bitshuba besipre haqqadosh rab pealim:

clarification.explanation: After reciting the blessing and separating, one says aloud “This is challah,” to give it a verbal designation after the blessing. And although many hold that no verbal designation is required, since there are eminent authorities who hold that it is, there is no loss in saying these three words, so as to satisfy all opinions.
takeaways: One says “This is challah” after the separation, so as to satisfy all opinions

paragraphs: Haro"sh za"l haya mishtaddel baasiyyat matztzat mitzva bikbodo ubeatzmo, veken rauy lekol adam laasot, veamar rabbenu haari"y za"l hammatricha atzmo bematztzat mitzva ad shemmazzia yoil letiqqun qeri, vehallash achar issur chametz yomar bitchillat hallisha kol perurin sheyyippelu bishat lisha vaarika, veken batzeq hannidbaq bekelim yihyu hepqer keapra deara, vehamminhag lehatznia hallulabin lehassiq bahem hattannur laapiyyat matztzat mitzva, vehinneh mitzvat mitzva zo mitzva min hammubchar lalush veleepot otah beereb pesach achar sheba umechetza veayyen birke yosep za"l:

clarification.explanation: The Rosh would exert himself to make matzat mitzvah with his own hands, and so is it fitting for every person to do. The Ari, of blessed memory, said that the exertion of sweating while making matzat mitzvah serves as a kabbalistic rectification for the flaw of “keri.” One who kneads after the prohibition of chametz has begun should declare at the start of the kneading that all crumbs that fall and dough that sticks to the vessels are ownerless like dust. The custom is to save lulav branches to fuel the oven, and it is best to knead and bake on the eve of Pesach after seven-thirty.
takeaways: It is fitting to make matzat mitzvah oneself, and to declare the crumbs ownerless
According to the Ari, of blessed memory, the sweat from the exertion of kneading serves as a kabbalistic rectification for the flaw of “keri”
It is best to knead and bake on the eve of Pesach after seven-thirty

paragraphs: Im nimtza chitta bammatztza beodah chayya, im enah mebuqqaat yiqqach min hammatztza kede netilat maqom, vehammatztza atzmah mutteret, veim hi mebuqqaat yeesor kol otah hammatztza shennimtzet bah hachitta abal em hachitta nimtzet baissa apillu mebuqqaat, notel bah kede netilat maqom bilbad vezoreqo laesh vekol haissa mutteret, mippene sheyyesh bazeh hepsed merubbeh vegam sheat haddechaq ukemo shekkatabti besipri haqqatan mqbtzyl:

clarification.explanation: If a wheat grain is found in the matzah while it is still raw and not split open, one removes the amount that occupied its space and the entire matzah is permitted; but if it is split open, the entire matzah in which it was found becomes forbidden. But if the grain is found in the dough [before baking], even if split open, one removes only the amount that occupied its space and throws it into the fire, and the entire batch of dough is permitted, because of the great loss involved and the pressing circumstance.
takeaways: A split wheat grain in a raw matzah forbids it; in the dough itself, only its own space is removed

paragraphs: Asur laasot melaka beereb pesach mechatzot ulemala apillu bechinnam. vetzarik lehistapper qodem chatzot, veim shakach qodem chatzot yistapper achar chatzot "y goy, ak tzarik sheyyaamid yisrael al gab lirot mittechillat tisporet ad hassop, vaapillu qetzitzat hatztzipparenayim tob lehizzaher laqutz otam qodem chatzot:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to perform work on the eve of Pesach from midday onward, even without payment. One must get a haircut before midday, and if he forgot, he may get one after midday through a non-Jew, provided a Jew stands over him and watches from the start of the haircut to its end. It is also good to cut one's fingernails before midday.
takeaways: No work on the eve of Pesach from midday onward; get a haircut and cut fingernails before midday

paragraphs: Habbekorot apillu hem kohanim o leviyyim mitannim beereb pesach ben bekor meab ben bekor meadam vedavqa hazzekarim abal hanneqebot lo nahagu lehitannot, vehazzakar apillu nolad achar nepel gam ken yitanneh, vehannolad achar valad shemmet tok sheloshim yom vekalu lo chodashayv lo yitanneh, deyesh lismok bazeh al haggaon shebut yaaqob vehaggaon dagul merebaba dimqillin bazeh, veim habbekor atzmo haya chatan o abi habben o sandaq muttar leekol veen tzarik liproa taanito achar hechag, abal im nizdammen lo pidyon sheppodeh et beno en leekol, veyesh nohagim dehechatan mazmin et habbekorot lisod bo bayyom etzlo bisudat chatan, veken abi habben bisudat mila veen anachnu mochin beyad hannohagim bekak, mihu eno yakol lehazmin harbeh ella raq tzimtzum lehashlim haasara velo yoter veayyen chaq yaaqob, ubisudat siyyum massekta im habbekor gamir vesabir lehannicha mah sheomerim beet hassiyyum muttar lo leekol sham veayyen chayyim lerosh:

clarification.explanation: Firstborns, even Kohanim and Levites, fast on the eve of Pesach - whether firstborn to the father or to the mother - but only males, not females. Even a male born after a stillbirth (a fetus whose months were not completed) must fast. But a male born after a child that completed its months and died within thirty days of birth need not fast, relying on the lenient authorities (the responsa Shevut Yaakov and the Dagul MeRevavah). If the firstborn is a groom, the father of a child [being circumcised], or a sandak, he may eat and need not make up the fast, but if he has a pidyon haben to perform he may not eat. Some have the custom that the groom invites firstborns to his feast, and likewise the father of the child at a brit feast, but only a limited number, enough to complete a minyan of ten. And likewise at a siyum masechet, if the firstborn understands what is said, he may eat there.
takeaways: Male firstborns fast on the eve of Pesach, including one born after a stillbirth
A male born after a child that completed its months and died within thirty days is exempt from the fast, per the lenient authorities
A firstborn participating in a se'udat mitzvah (wedding, brit, siyum) is exempt from the fast

paragraphs: Asur lomar basar zeh lepesach, ella yomar basar zeh leyom tob, veasur leekol matztza beereb pesach, vegam ballayla shel ereb pesach en leekol, abal matztza mebushshelet shebbishshelah qodem y"d muttar leekol by"d, ken haaleti bitshuba bs"d besipre haqqadosh rab pealim, velo yokal harbeh beereb pesach, kede sheyyokal belel pesach leteabon mashal lemi sheyyizdammen etzlo oreach veku':

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to say “this meat is for Pesach,” rather “this meat is for Yom Tov.” It is forbidden to eat matzah on the eve of Pesach, and also on the night before it, but cooked matzah that was cooked before the fourteenth is permitted to be eaten on the fourteenth. And one should not eat much on the eve of Pesach, so as to eat on Seder night with appetite.
takeaways: One does not say “meat for Pesach” but “for Yom Tov”
Matzah is not eaten on the eve of Pesach; and one does not eat much, so as to eat at the Seder with appetite

paragraphs: Yizzaharu hannashim bibdiqat hachzarat vehakkarpas, dekol tola yesh bo chiyyub chamishsha milleqiyyot, vehaddabar hazzeh taluy betzavvar haishsha baalat habbayit dekol bene habbayit somekin aleha bazeh, veim meqilla bibdiqa epshar sheyyihyeh taluy betzavvarah chiyyub malqot yoter missearot roshah, biprat bihyot bene habbayit merubbin ubimqomot ellu shehattolaim qetannim metzuyim harbeh biraqot, maaseh bechakam echad shenniknas beereb pesach lechatzer echad, veraa et haishsha baalat habbayit, lepaneha shene sallim gedolim meleim chazeret, vehi rochetzet healim shel hachzarat veroeh otam bimhirut kilachar yad uminchat besal lepaneha veyomar lah hechakam: kamma searot yesh beroshka, amera lo lo maniti otam ulepi dati i epshar limnotam, amar lah searot roshka epshar lehimmanot, ak chiyyub hammalquyyot asher betzavvarka i epshar lehimmanot, amera lo ma eeseh bene habbayit merubbin verotzin leekol chazeret harbeh ki arab lahem, amar lah teshuba zo lo tatztzilek beyom haddin, al ken shimi laatzati vetashliki healin shetztzarik lahem bediqa merubbeh, vetiqqechi haqqelachim davqa veken hakkarpas tibbadeqi lahem shiur muat latzet yede choba davqa. al ken bayit sheokelayv merubbin veen bodeqim harbeh yaasu ken, venohagim shello leekol chazeret beereb pesach, veken bechutz laaretz en okelim chazeret beyom rishon shel pesach:

clarification.explanation: Women must be very careful in checking lettuce and celery for insects, since any insect carries a liability of five lashes, and the members of the household rely on the woman of the house in this. A story is brought of a sage who rebuked a woman who checked leaves quickly, telling her that the liability of lashes hanging over her neck exceeds the hairs of her head, and he advised her to discard the leaves requiring extensive checking and take only the stalks. Therefore, in a household with many diners where thorough checking is not done, one should do the same. And the custom is not to eat lettuce on the eve of Pesach.
takeaways: Lettuce and celery are checked well for insects
In a large household - it is preferable to take stalks instead of leaves; lettuce is not eaten on the eve of Pesach

paragraphs: Yihyeh shulchano aruk mibbeod yom kede sheyyeqaddesh miyyad keshettechshak dehaynu achar tzet hakkokabim, veyishteh bahasibba kol arbaa kosot, vekullam tzerikin meziga veyaaseh hammeziga bemayim beshalosh pesaqot zo achar zo, ubaal habbayit yimzog lo hakkos echad mibbene habbayit derek cherut, gam yeqabbel hakkos bishte yadayv mishte yadayv shel hannoten, gam akilat kol arba kezayyatot shel matztza yihyu bahasibba ben anashim uben hannashim ben haggedolim ben haqqetannim, vehahasibba tzerika lihyot al tzad semol, vaapillu itter meseb al semol kol adam udelo keman dekatab lehepek:

clarification.explanation: His table should be set from before nightfall so he can recite Kiddush immediately when it grows dark, after the stars come out. All four cups are drunk while reclining, and all require dilution with water in three separate pourings. The head of the household has his cup poured by a household member in a manner expressing freedom, and receives it with both hands from the giver's two hands. The eating of the four ke-zayit portions of matzah is likewise done while reclining - by men, women, adults, and children alike - and the reclining is on the left side, even for a left-handed person.
takeaways: The four cups and the matzah are eaten reclining on the left side
The cups are poured and received in a manner of freedom; even a left-handed person reclines on the left

paragraphs: Tzarik lishtot rob harebiit bebat achat dehaynu shetiyya achat velo yapsiqennu bishte shetiyyot, ubediabad apillu hipsiq kamma peamim yatza, veraq lo yishheh mittechillat shetiyya ad hassop yoter mikkede shetiyyat rebiit, umishqal harebiit hu esrim vesheba drh"m, ulekattechilla tzarik sheyyishteh kol harebiit, ak bediabad im shata rob rebiit yatza yede chobato, vekannizkar bapposeqim, v"g dibraka acharona en lebarek beshoteh rob rebiit, mishshum deyesh bazeh pelugta vesapeq berakot lehaqel, im kol zeh belel pesach deikka d' kosot uberaka acharona shayeka lekullehu, im bechad minnayhu o bitre shata rebiit shalem, yukal lebarek aach"k beraka acharona, abal im lo shata beshum chad rebiit shalem lo yebarek beraka acharona al hayyayin desapeq berakot lehaqel, al ken yidchoq atzmo lepachot bekos echad lishtot rebiit shalem, veim yesh bakkos kamma rebiiyyot tzarik lishtot rubbo, vekol haarba kosot tzerikin shetipa vahadacha sheyyirchatzem mibbayit umichutz bekol paam:

clarification.explanation: One must drink most of the revi'it in one go, without a break, and after the fact he has fulfilled his obligation even if he paused, provided he did not take longer overall than the time it takes to drink a revi'it (the weight of a revi'it is twenty-seven dirhams). As a preferred practice one drinks the whole revi'it, and after the fact, most of it. Regarding the concluding blessing: on Pesach night, if he drank a full revi'it in one of the cups, he blesses afterward; if he did not drink a full revi'it in any cup, he does not bless. Therefore he should push himself to drink at least one full revi'it in one cup. All the cups require rinsing and washing each time.
takeaways: Most of the revi'it is drunk in one go, without a break
One should take care to drink at least a full revi'it in one cup, for the sake of the concluding blessing

paragraphs: Mebiin lipne baal habbayit qeara sheyyesh bah shelosha matztzot umaror vacharoset vekarpas uzeroa ubetza, vehacharoset zeker lattit shennishtabedu bo abotenu, lekak mannichim betoko egozim usheqedim, vehazzeroa zeker lepesach debizman bet hammiqdash haya mebi gam et happesach bishat amirat hahaggada, vehabbetza zeker leqarebban chagiga, uminhagenu laasot hazzeroa tzali vehabbetza sheluqa bemayim, veim shakach velo tzala hazzeroa beereb pesach muttar litzloto belel pesach, "g deen okelin tzali gam beyom rishon ukemo shekkatabti besipri haqqatan mqbtzyl, utzerikin lehizzaher bekol betzim sheshsholeqin biqdera bepesach sheyyirchatzu techilla bemayim tzonenin betok keli echad bipne atzman, mippene ki etzlenu ellu hammokerim et habbetzim qonim otam min haarbiyyim vehem mannichim otam im haqqemachim shellahem venidbaq al qelippatam qemach, lekak yerachatzum heteb techilla ki chametz bepesach bemashshehu:

clarification.explanation: They bring before the head of the household a plate with three matzot, maror, charoset, karpas, a zeroa, and an egg. The charoset is a remembrance of the mortar of the enslavement, so nuts and almonds are placed in it; the zeroa is a remembrance of the Pesach offering, and the egg a remembrance of the chagigah offering. Our custom is to roast the zeroa and boil the egg. If he forgot to roast the zeroa before Pesach, it is permitted to roast it on Pesach night. One must be careful to wash all the eggs boiled during Pesach first, in cold water in a separate vessel, since flour sometimes sticks to their shells and chametz on Pesach is forbidden even in the tiniest amount.
takeaways: The Seder plate is arranged with three matzot, maror, charoset, karpas, zeroa, and an egg
The eggs are washed of flour before cooking

paragraphs: Notel yadayv letzorek tibbul rishon velo yebarek al netila zo, veashre hannizhar littol yadayv betibbul mashqeh bekol hashshana kullah, vaateret rashe harab mor abi zlh"h haya nizhar bekol hashshana vehaya mazhir lekamma bene adam bazeh ki beemet minhag haolam lehaqel bazeh bishar yemot hashshana hu banuy al sebara yechidaa veayyen beshu"t matteh yosep za"l mah shekkatab bazeh:

clarification.explanation: One washes his hands for the first dipping and does not recite a blessing over this washing. Praiseworthy is one who is careful to wash his hands before eating any food dipped in liquid throughout the entire year, as the author's father was careful and would warn others about this, since the common leniency in this matter during the rest of the year is based on a solitary opinion.
takeaways: Hands are washed for the first dipping, without a blessing
It is fitting to be careful about washing hands for [food] dipped in liquid all year round

paragraphs: Yiqqach karpas pachot mikkazzayit, shello yitchayyeb bibraka acharona vibarek alayv bore peri haadama, vikavven liptor hammaror veyitbol oto bechometz veyoklennu belo hasibba, ukemo shekkatab haggaon chida" za"l veken minhagenu mizzeman ateret rashe harab haggaon mor zeqeni zlh"h leakelo belo hasibba, vetibbul rishon zeh shehu karpas bechometz, hu zakar lesibbat qoshi hashshibud shehaya bishbil mekirat yosep hatztzaddiq alayv hashshalom veshehitbilu ketonet passim shello baddam umekaruhu vegaremu tzaar leyaaqob abinu alayv hashshalom, vezeh nirmaz bekarpas vehaynu otiyyot "kar" hem sop meker veotiyyot "pas" hem rosh "passim", vetibbul sheni shehu maror bacharoset hu zeker laqqoshi hashshibud atzmo shemmereru chayyehem bemaaseh hattit haramuz bacharoset ukemo shekkatabti bazeh besipri haqqatan mqbtzyl v"g sheamarnu shetztzarik liqqach karpas pachot mikkazzayit kede shello yitchayyeb bibraka acharona hinneh im shaga veakal kazzayit tzarik lebarek acharayv bore nepashot rabbot, veim kol zeh lo yebarek al hammaror bore peri haadama yaan dachashib mitztzareke hasseuda habbaim tok hasseuda, veyizzaher shello yokal kol hakkarpas sheyyesh baqqeara ella yishshaer baqqeara mehakkarpas ad achar hammotzi, detzarik sheyyihyeh sod haqqeara shalem ad leachar akilat matztza umaror:

clarification.explanation: One takes karpas less than a ke-zayit so as not to become obligated in a concluding blessing, blesses “Borei peri ha'adamah” and intends to exempt the maror as well, dips it in vinegar, and eats it without reclining. The first dipping - karpas in vinegar - is a remembrance of the harsh servitude that came about through the sale of Joseph (“kar” being the end of “mechar” - sale, and “pas” the beginning of “passim” - the coat of many colors), and the second dipping (maror in charoset) is a remembrance of the servitude itself. If he mistakenly ate a ke-zayit of karpas, he must recite “Borei nefashot” afterward; nevertheless he should not recite “Borei peri ha'adamah” over the maror, since it is considered among the requirements of the meal that come within it. He should be careful to leave some karpas on the plate until after HaMotzi, since the “secret of the plate” must remain intact until after the eating of matzah and maror.
takeaways: Karpas less than a ke-zayit, “Borei peri ha'adamah” with intent to exempt the maror, without reclining
Some karpas is left on the plate until after HaMotzi, and the “secret of the plate” remains intact until after the eating of matzah and maror

paragraphs: Yiqqach matztza haemtzait vichalleqenna lishtayim, veyitten chetzyah haggadol leechad mehamsubbin lehatznio laapiqoman, vachatzi hashsheni haqqatan yannicha ben shette hammatztzot hashshelemot, ukepi hassod yechalleqenna lehaemtzait tzurat "d" "v" vetziro shel v' yannicha laapiqoman vetzurat d' yannicha ben hammatztzot ukesheomer ha lachma aneya yagbihha biprusa, veyomar ha btzyr"y, uminhagenu likpol pisqa zo shalosh peamim, veaach"k yetzavveh lehannicha haqqeara besop hashshulchan, gam yimzegu hakkos veyannichu lepanayv kede sheyyishalu veyomru "mah nishtanna", ukesheyyatchil lomar abadim maggishim haqqeara lepanayv, ukesheomer en maptirin achar happesach apiqoman minhag yapeh leechoz chatzi hammatztza hattemuna laapiqoman leharot libne hammesibba shehu zeker lepesach vekannizkar beseper tanya, ukeshemmaggia l"matztza zo", yagbihha hammatztza hashshelema haelyona shellepanayv lechibbub mitzva, veken hu haddin kesheyyaggia lemaror zeh, abal kesheamur "pesach shehayu abotenu okelin" lo yeechoz hazzeroa beyado ella yirennu bilbad, ukesheyyaggia lehi sheameda, yeechoz beyado hakkos shemmezago lo, vikasseh happat, veyizzaher lekassot happat bekol et shelloqeach hakkos beyado:

clarification.explanation: He takes the middle matzah and divides it in two: the larger half is given to be put away for the afikoman, and the smaller placed between the two whole matzot. And according to the kabbalistic secret, he divides the middle matzah so as to form the shape of two letters - dalet and vav: the piece shaped like the vav is set aside for the afikoman, and the piece shaped like the dalet remains between the matzot. When he says “Ha lachma anya” he lifts the broken piece, and says “Ha” with a tzeirei (and our custom is to repeat this passage three times). Afterward he instructs that the plate be placed at the end of the table, and the cup poured and placed before him so that the children will ask “Mah Nishtanah”; and when he begins “Avadim hayinu,” the plate is brought before him again. And when he says “Ein maftirin achar hapesach afikoman,” it is a fine custom to hold up the half-matzah hidden for the afikoman and show it to those present as a remembrance of the Pesach offering. When he reaches “Matzah zo” and “Maror zeh,” he lifts them up, but the zeroa (in the passage about the Pesach offering) he only shows, without holding it up. And when he reaches “Hi she'amdah” he holds the cup, and covers the bread - and one should remember to cover the bread whenever the cup is held.
takeaways: The dividing of the middle matzah is done according to the kabbalistic secret, forming the shape of the letters dalet-vav: the vav-piece for the afikoman, and the dalet-piece remaining between the matzot
The broken piece is lifted up while reciting “Ha lachma anya,” and the custom is to repeat this passage three times
At “Matzah zo” and “Maror zeh,” these are lifted up; the zeroa (in the passage about the Pesach offering) is only shown, without lifting
Whenever the cup is held (as at “Hi she'amdah”), one must remember to cover the bread

paragraphs: Yittol yadayv vibarek al netilat yadayim, veyiqqach hammatztzot shelashettam beyachad mishshum lechem mishneh, vibarek hammotzi veyashmit hashshelishit veyishshaer beyado matztza haelyona vehapperusa, vibarek al akilat matztza veyibtza mehaelyona vehapperusa kazzayit mizzo vekazzayit mizzo, vekol kazzayit hu tisha drh"m, veyitbelem bemelach shalosh peamim veyoklem bahasibba, veyaknis shette kezayyatot ellu bepiv beyachad, kede sheyyokal mishshenehem bebat achat veim yesh lo ones sheeno yakol laasot ken veyirtzeh liprer kol kazzayit perurin qetannim lehaknisam bepiv, az yaknis perure kazzayit hashshelema techilla vekannizkar baacharonim. veaach"k yiqqach kazzayit maror vishaqqeennu bacharoset, vinaer meat min hacharoset debae taam maror, vibarek al akilat maror veen tzarik hasibba, veaach"k tekep notel matztza hashshelishit ubotzea kazzayit mimmenna vekoreko im kazzayit maror umetabbel bacharoset, veomer "zeker lammiqdash kehillel hazzaqen veku'" veyoklem bahasibba, veyizzaher shello yedabber debarim chitzonim ben akilat matztza laakilat hakkorek, velaken yoklem bezeh achar zeh tekep belo ikkub, veaach"k soed vegomer seuddato besimcha ubetub lebab:

clarification.explanation: He washes his hands with a blessing, takes the three matzot together for the sake of “lechem mishneh,” recites “HaMotzi,” sets aside the third, and recites “concerning the eating of matzah” over the top matzah and the broken one. He breaks off a ke-zayit from each (a ke-zayit being nine dirhams), dips them in salt three times, and eats them together while reclining. Afterward he eats a ke-zayit of maror dipped in charoset (shaking off a little of the charoset so the taste of maror remains), recites “concerning the eating of maror,” without reclining. Then he immediately takes a ke-zayit from the third matzah, wraps it with maror and charoset, says “A remembrance of the Beit HaMikdash, in the manner of Hillel,” and eats it while reclining, without speaking between the eating of the matzah and the korech.
takeaways: HaMotzi and matzah are eaten as two ke-zayit portions while reclining; maror dipped in charoset is eaten without reclining
The korech is eaten while reclining, immediately, without speaking between the matzah and the korech

paragraphs: Achar sheggamar seuddato yokal besimcha et haapiqoman hashshamur betok hammappa zeker lepesach hanneekol al hishshaba, velaken yizzaher shello yokal harbeh betok hasseuda kede sheyyokal haapiqoman leteabon, veyokal mimmennu shette kezayyatot lemitzva min hammubchar, shehem: kazzayit echad zeker lappesach vekazzayit echad zeker lammatztza hanneekelet im happesach, veim hu zaqen o chalush meod veqasheh alayv leekol shette kazzayyatot yokal kazzayit echad davqa zeker lepesach, vetzarik leekol oto bemaqom echad, velo bishte meqomot, vaapillu becheder echad bishte shulchanot asur, veyizzaher leakelo qodem chatzot, vetob sheggam hahallel yomar qodem chatzot, velo yitnamnem beemtza akilat haapiqoman, veim hu meseb lebaddo al hashshulchan apillu betok hasseuda qodem akilat haapiqoman lo yashan veayyen shulchan gabohha za"l: achar haapiqoman en leekol shum dabar, mishshum debainan sheyyihyeh taam haapiqoman bepiv ad sheyyashen, veraq mayim muttar lishtot, veyesh mattirin bqhvv" (qapeh) veyesh lismok alehem letzorek gadol, ushetiyyat ashan, sham hiskim harab chayyim palagi'y b"chayyim lerosh" lehazhir belel rishon, abal belel sheni hittir, umah sheqqorin oto apiqoman hu nateriqon appiqu mine shello yoklu od, vaateret rashe harab mor abi zlh"h peresh appiqu m"n - rashe tebot "miyyayin nuqbin" haolin min mitzvat akilat matztza vaakila zo hi mitzva acharona vedibra pi chakamim chen:

clarification.explanation: After the meal, he joyfully eats the afikoman that was kept, as a remembrance of the Pesach offering eaten while satiated; therefore he should not eat much during the meal, so as to eat the afikoman with appetite. He eats two ke-zayit portions (one for the Pesach offering, one for the matzah eaten with it), and an elderly or very weak person eats one ke-zayit, specifically for the Pesach offering. He eats it in one place, before midnight, and does not doze off in the middle. After the afikoman nothing is eaten, so that its taste remains in his mouth until he falls asleep; only water may be drunk (and some permit coffee for great need), and smoking - forbidden on the first night, permitted on the second. The name “afikoman” is explained as a Greek-derived acronym for “afiku minei” (do not eat anything else), and the author's father explained it as “afiku man” - an acronym for “mayin nukvin” arising from the mitzvah of eating this matzah, the final mitzvah.
takeaways: The afikoman (two ke-zayit portions) is eaten in one place, before midnight, with appetite
Nothing is eaten afterward; only water is permitted (some permit coffee); smoking is forbidden on the first night and permitted on the second
The name “afikoman” is expounded as a Greek-derived acronym: “afiku minei” (do not eat any more), and also “afiku man” - an acronym for “mayin nukvin”

paragraphs: Im shakach velo akal haapiqoman ad shennatal yadayv, o amar "hab lan unebarek", yokal oto belo birkat hammotzi, veim lo nizkar ad shebberak birkat hammazon im lo shata kos shelishi, yittol yadayv vibarek hammotzi veyokal haapiqoman, veim shata kos shelishi veaach"k nizkar, hinneh im akal tok hasseuda mizzot hammatztza hashshemura mishsheat qetzira shiur kazzayit somek al zeh, veim lav az illu im lo nizkar ella ad achar hahallel yittol yadayv vibarek hammotzi veyokal haapiqoman, veyachazor vibarek al hakkos, veayyen bet david siman rn"t dap ' veshulchan gabohha siman t"v seip qatan ch yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: If one forgot to eat the afikoman and remembered after washing his hands or saying “Hav lan u'nevareich,” he eats it without the blessing of HaMotzi. If he remembered after Grace after Meals but before the third cup, he washes his hands, recites HaMotzi, and eats it. If he had already drunk the third cup, and he ate a ke-zayit of shmurah matzah during the meal, he may rely on that; if not, and he only remembered after the Hallel, he washes his hands, recites HaMotzi, eats the afikoman, and then returns to recite the blessing over the cup.
takeaways: Forgetting the afikoman - the order of correction depends on whether he has already recited Grace after Meals or drunk the third cup

paragraphs: Chayyab adam lesapper benissim veniplaot sheasa hashshem yitbarak lanu velaabotenu ad shettikrachanu hashshena lishon, veita bazzohar haqqadosh (r"m parashat ba) peqoda lesapper bitziat mitzrayim veku' vequdesha berik hu chade behay sippura, vkn"sh lekol pamalya shel mala, vaamar lehon zilo shimu hay shebacha diltatta, ubehay sippura baqei reqiayya veyahabi chela lemearyehon, ubazeh kelal hammarbeh lesapper bitziat mitzrayim hare zeh meshubbach beppamalya shello maaleh shqb"h mishtabbeach bo kediktib (yeshaya mt, g) "yisrael asher beka etpaar":

clarification.explanation: A person is obligated to recount the miracles and wonders that God performed for us and our forefathers, until sleep overtakes him. The holy Zohar teaches that the Holy One rejoices in this recounting and gathers the heavenly retinue to hear the praise of Israel from below, and through this recounting the heavens are split open and strength is granted above. Therefore, one who recounts much of the Exodus is praiseworthy, for the Holy One glories in him.
takeaways: One recounts the Exodus until overcome by sleep
One who recounts much is praiseworthy - the Holy One glories in Israel

paragraphs: Tzarik lomar qeriat shema al hammitta im happesuqim hannohagim bekol layla keseder rabbenu haari"y za"l, veim hu neor ad achar chatzot yomar otah meat qodem chatzot, ubachutz laaretz kol hilkot layla rishona noheget belayla sheniyya, utzeri lebarek shehecheyanu bechutz laaretz bishte lelot harishonim shel pesach beqiddush, abal ballelot haacharonim shehem yom shebii veyom shemini shel pesach en mebarekin shehecheyanu beqiddush, ukesheomerim shehecheyanu ballayla harishona yekavven gam al akilat matztza:

clarification.explanation: One recites the Shema on retiring with the verses customary every night, in the order of the Ari, of blessed memory; if he stays awake past midnight he should recite it a little before midnight. Outside the Land, all the laws of the first night apply also to the second night, and Shehecheyanu is recited at Kiddush on both of the first two nights, but not on the last nights (the seventh and eighth days). When reciting Shehecheyanu on the first night, one should also intend it for the eating of matzah.
takeaways: The Shema on retiring follows the order of the Ari
Outside the Land, Shehecheyanu is recited only on the first two nights; one intends it also for the matzah

paragraphs: Haubbar lipne hannachtom goy bepesach velo yaricha mippat cham, umatzati katub deen makkin hakkelabim bechag happesach ubiprat beyom ' ubeyom b' shebbahem mesapperim bitziat mitzrayim, v"p sheameru rabbotenu za"l al hakkeleb (shabbat qeneh:) "meshach udneh vechutra abbatereh", mesirin hachutera mealehem bepesach ki belel pesach bitziat mitzrayim ketib lo yecheratz keleb leshono sheshshameru gezerato yitbarek beotah hallayla, delaken amera tora al nebela lekeleb tashlikun oto:

clarification.explanation: One passing by a non-Jew's bakery on Pesach should not smell the hot bread. And it is found written that dogs are not struck during the festival of Pesach, especially on the first and second days, since on the night of the Exodus it is written “no dog shall whet its tongue” - the dogs observed God's decree on that night; therefore the Torah says regarding an unfit carcass, “You shall throw it to the dog.”
takeaways: One does not smell hot bread from a non-Jew on Pesach
The custom is not to strike dogs on Pesach, as a reward for their restraint on the night of the Exodus

paragraphs: Yashgichu mokere hatztzimmuqim besaqqim shellahem shello yihyeh besaqqim chametz beayin - shedderakim lihyot dabeq bahem chametz, mechamat shebbammaqom hahu shel hatztzimmuqim darkam lehishtammesh bahem beqemach uba alehem mayim umitlaklek hassaq baqqemach shennaasa chametz beayin, vehamgaddel tarnegolim yebarer hallul shellahem mehasseorim, veyiqneh lahem qodem pesach dochan o zavvera (dora) veyatchil lehaakilam mizzeh qodem sheyyikkanes happesach, umuttar liqnot tarnegolim betok happesach veyomar beperush sheeno rotzeh liqnot hazzepeq kelal, veachar shechita yiptachenna tekep veyashlik zepeq lachutz, veayyen beshiyyure beraka ubetub ayin, upoh irenu yesh kamma baale battim sheen okelim tarnegolim bepesach mishshum gader useyag dechosheshin pen yimmatze behahem chittin useorim, veharotzeh leekol tarnegolim mippene sheyyesh lo sibba hekrechit yaaseh hattara al minhag shello vekannizkar beleb chayyim cheleq b' siman r"z:

clarification.explanation: Raisin sellers should watch that their sacks contain no actual chametz, since flour is used where the raisins are kept and can become chametz when moistened. One who raises chickens should clear their coop of barley and feed them millet or sorghum before Pesach. It is permitted to buy chickens during Pesach, provided one states he does not wish to buy the crop [gizzard] at all, and throws it out immediately after slaughtering. Some householders in this city do not eat chicken at all during Pesach as a protective measure, out of concern for wheat or barley in the crop, and one who wishes to eat it for a pressing reason should have his personal custom annulled.
takeaways: The chicken coop is cleared of barley and the birds are fed sorghum before Pesach
One who buys a chicken during Pesach stipulates not buying the crop, and discards it immediately

paragraphs: Poh irenu yesh harbeh baale battim nohagim shello leekol orez bepesach mippene ki haorez yimmatze bo taarobet chittin useorim, vetzarik lebadeqo techilla paamayim veshalosh, vechosheshin shemma yishgu bibdiqa, veyishshaer beorez chitta useora vibashshelu bo lekak bedelin mimmennu, veyesh nohagin leekol achar bediqa, al ken im baal habbayit okel orez vehambashshel shello noheg sheeno okel orez asur lebashshel orez beyom tob lebaal habbayit kevan dehu noheg issur baakilato mishshum gader useyag, abal letaltelo beyom tob muttar, ken heeleti bs"d bitshuba besipre haqqadosh rab pealim, vehaddomeh ledin zeh timtza gam bishar yeme tobim sheim zeh hambashshel akal basar beyom tob, asur lebashshel chalab laacherim ella im ken yesh shehut bayyom sheyyaabor zeman shesh shaot achar akilat habbasar kede sherauy sheyyokal zeh min hattabshil hahu bo bayyom, abal im en shehut bayyom sheyyokal hu atzmo mimmennu asur lebashshel laacherim, mihu betiltul shari:

clarification.explanation: In Baghdad many have the custom not to eat rice on Pesach out of concern for a mixture of wheat and barley that is difficult to check for, and some have the custom of eating it after checking. Therefore, if the head of the household eats rice but the cook observes a prohibition against it, it is forbidden for the cook to cook rice on Yom Tov for the head of the household (though carrying it is permitted). The same applies on other Yom Tovim: a cook who ate meat may not cook dairy for others unless there remains enough time in the day for him to eat from that dish himself after six hours have passed - but carrying it is permitted.
takeaways: The custom in Baghdad is to abstain from rice on Pesach out of concern for a mixture
One who personally observes a prohibition does not cook that same food for another, though carrying it is permitted

paragraphs: Lo yishtu chalab mibbehemat goy bepesach shemma heekil otah chametz, veim loqechim seor min haggoy achar happesach yezahu lehaprish meotah issa challa shettihyeh gedola mishshiur hasseor kullo:

clarification.explanation: One does not drink milk from a non-Jew's animal on Pesach, lest he fed it chametz. And if leaven is taken from a non-Jew after Pesach, one should be careful to separate from that dough a challah larger than the measure of the entire leaven.
takeaways: Milk from a non-Jew's animal is not drunk on Pesach
Leaven from a non-Jew after Pesach - a challah portion larger than the whole leaven is separated

paragraphs: En omerim tiqqun lea bechol hammoed shel pesach veyizzaharu bekol yeme hammoed laasoq battora hannotenet chayyim leoseha baolam hazzeh ubaolam habba:

clarification.explanation: Tikkun Leah (Tikkun Chatzot) is not recited during Chol HaMoed of Pesach. One should be careful throughout all the days of the festival to occupy oneself with Torah, which gives life to those who practice it, in this world and the next.
takeaways: Tikkun Leah is not recited during Chol HaMoed of Pesach
One occupies oneself with Torah throughout all the days of the festival

paragraphs: Bodeqin belel y"g kepi hahalakot shekkatabnu leel bibdiqa shel lel y"d, vehabbekorot mitannim beyom chamishi, al ken im habbodeq hu bekor yitom qodem habberaka perot o mine mezonot, kede sheyyibdoq beyishshub haddaat ubenachat, veachar habbediqa yebattel hechametz kemo shekkatabnu belel y"d, abal bittul shel hayyom lo yebattel beyom shishshi ella yebattel beyom shabbat, veyizzaher shello yishkachehu, ak biur chametz yaasehu beyom shishshi sheyyisrop happetitim sheeno rotzeh leakelam, umeshayyer happat letzorek seudat lel shabbat useudat shacharit deshabbat, vehabbiur beereb pesach yaasehu qodem chatzot kederek sheoseh by"d keshechal bechol, kede shello yabou litot bishar shanim:

clarification.explanation: When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbat, one checks for chametz on the night of the thirteenth, following the same laws as the search on the night of the fourteenth. The firstborns fast on Thursday. If the searcher is a firstborn, he should taste fruit or grain-based food before the blessing, so as to search calmly. After the search he nullifies the chametz, but he does not perform the daytime nullification on Friday - rather on Shabbat itself (and he should be careful not to forget). The burning is done on Friday before midday, setting aside bread for the Shabbat meals.
takeaways: When Erev Pesach falls on Shabbat: the search is on the night of the thirteenth; firstborns fast on Thursday
The burning is done on Friday before midday; the daytime nullification is postponed to Shabbat

paragraphs: Beyom shabbat qodem shehu yom y"d yemaharu lehitpallel babboqer kede latzet bimhera leekol seudat shacharit shello yikkashelu beissur akilat chametz beereb pesach achar hazzeman ak yizzaharu shello yitpallelu bechippazon ubimrutza, veim yesh chatanim beoto shabbat lo yazminu abot habbanim orechim harbeh letzorek aliyyat seper tora kedarkan, kede shello lehaarik hazzeman bekak, shetztzarik latzet mehera leekol seudat shacharit vimaharu leqaddesh veleekol tekep, veyoklu kol chametz sheyyesh etzlam bayit qodem sheyyachul issur akilato, veim nishar chametz sheen yekolim leakelo yittenuhu legoy, velo yizreqennu lirshut harabbim, veen mibbeshilin leshabbat zo tabshil sheddarko lihyot dabeq harbeh baqqedera shello yitqannach beetzba, kede shello yitztarek lehaddicha haqqederot vehaqqearot mihu im bishshel kazeh venidbaq hattabshil baqqedera muttar lehaddicha haqqedera bemayim beyado, abal lo bismartut mishshum issur sechita beshabbat, vahadacha zo nechshebet qetzat tzorek hayyom deikka bazeh tzorek mitzva kemo shekkatebu happeri chadash ukeneset haggedola veshulchan gabohha, veim epshar leqannecho beetzba asur lehadicha kannizkar beeliyya raba ushear acharonim, veachar sheyyigmor kol akilato velo yishshaer etzlo chametz az yebattelennu veyomar kol chamira veku' dachaziteh udela chaziteh:

clarification.explanation: On the Shabbat that is the 14th, one hastens to pray in the morning in order to go out quickly to the morning meal, so as not to stumble into eating chametz after its permitted time (but without praying in haste). If there are grooms [being called up], the fathers should not invite many guests for the aliyot, so as not to prolong the service. They hasten to recite Kiddush and eat, finishing all their chametz before its prohibition takes effect; what remains is given to a non-Jew, not thrown into the public domain. On this Shabbat one should not cook a dish that sticks greatly to the pot; if it does stick, it is permitted to rinse the pot with water by hand (not with a rag, due to the prohibition of wringing). After finishing all his eating, with no chametz remaining, he nullifies it.
takeaways: One hastens to pray and eat before the time the chametz prohibition takes effect
One does not cook a dish that sticks to the pot; the chametz is nullified after the meal

paragraphs: Yokal seudat hallayla veshel shacharit beshabbat zo bechatzer bemaqom echad davqa, velo yaasu ballayla ubeshacharit perurin harbeh al hashshulchan, veim naasa perurin yashgicha alehem leakelam tekep qodem sheyyippol alehem mashqeh veyimmaasu, veachar akilatam yinaru hashshulchan o hammappa birshut harabbim, bishbil perurin qetannim sheen nilqatim bayyad leakelam, gam od achar akila yekabbedu hammaqom sheakelu bo mishshum ezeh perurin shennapelu, veyashlik hazzebel lirshut harabbim velo yannicha hazzebel baashpa shebbachatzero, umuttar leekol betzim beshabbat zo beshacharit veen chashash bazeh mishshum akilat betzim belel pesach deen zeh domeh lachazeret vekayyotze, ak yesh nohagim shello leekol beshabbat zo betzim beshacharit mippene shemmannichim betza belel pesach biqara veokelim otah zeker leqarebban chagiga vekol echad yaaseh keminhago bedabar zeh:

clarification.explanation: The night meal and morning meal on this Shabbat are eaten in one place only, and one should avoid making many crumbs; if crumbs are made, they are watched and eaten immediately. After eating, the table or cloth is shaken out into the public domain, and the eating place is swept, with the sweepings thrown into the public domain rather than left in the courtyard's trash heap. It is permitted to eat eggs at the morning meal on this Shabbat, though some abstain because an egg is placed on the Seder plate as a remembrance of the chagigah offering - and everyone follows his own custom.
takeaways: Eating in one place, and being careful to clean up all crumbs of chametz
It is permitted to eat eggs at the morning meal; some abstain, following their custom

paragraphs: Bigde moed yelabbeshum beshabbat zo achar mincha, vegam hakkuttonet yachalipu otah achar mincha mippene sheakal chametz ballayla ubeshacharit bihyotah alayv, vechosheshin shemma dabaq bah ezeh perur qatan shel chametz, abal bemiknasayim vetallit en chashash zeh, umi shehu ani veen lo ella kuttonet achat shellabesha belel shabbat yizzaher beet akilato litchob bet-yad shel hakkuttonet lipnim veachar akilato yibdoq kuttanetto:

clarification.explanation: Festival garments are put on this Shabbat after Minchah, and one also changes his shirt after Minchah, since chametz was eaten while wearing it and a small crumb might have stuck to it; but there is no such concern regarding trousers and a tallit. A poor person who has only one shirt should tuck the sleeve inward while eating, and check the shirt afterward.
takeaways: One changes the shirt and puts on festival garments after Minchah
A poor person with only one shirt tucks in the sleeve and checks it after eating

paragraphs: Seuda shelishit yaasenna beperot achar mincha, vetob laasotah beperot shebbirkatan meen shalosh, vaybium lepanayv baqqeara al hashshulchan veyomar gam ken qodem sheyyokal atqinu seudeta veku' kishar shabbat, velo yarbeh baakilato kede sheyyokal ballayla leteabon, ubazeh hashshabbat minhagi lidrosh beezrat Adonai bebet hakkeneset al hahaggada, ak tzarik lehaqdim kede shennitpallel betesha umechetza uderush shabbat haggadol hu bashshabbat haqqodem:

clarification.explanation: The third meal is made with fruit after Minchah, preferably fruit whose concluding blessing is “Me'ein Shalosh.” It is brought on a plate, with “Atkinu se'udata” recited as on any Shabbat, without eating much, so as to eat at night with appetite. On this Shabbat the author's custom is to expound in the synagogue on the Haggadah (beginning the prayers early, at nine-thirty), while the sermon proper for Shabbat HaGadol is given on the preceding Shabbat.
takeaways: The third meal is fruit (preferably “Me'ein Shalosh”) after Minchah, without eating much

paragraphs: Matztzat mitzva sheyyotze bah yede chobato belayla rishona lo yetaltelenna beyom shabbat zeh shechal beereb pesach, ki muqtzim hem dela chazu lemekal minnayhu devadday qaped lehaakil lattinoqot, abal shear matztzot shehem letzorek okelo bime happesach muttar letaltelam beshabbat zo, d"g dehaggedolim asurim leekol matztza beereb pesach, mikkol maqom chazu lemekal liqtannim:

clarification.explanation: The matzat mitzvah for the first night's obligation should not be moved on this Shabbat, since it is muktzeh, being unfit to eat (as one is certainly careful not to feed it even to children). But the other matzot, meant for eating during Pesach, are permitted to be moved on this Shabbat, since even though adults may not eat matzah on the eve of Pesach, it is fit for children to eat.
takeaways: The matzat mitzvah is muktzeh and forbidden to be moved on this Shabbat
The other matzot are permitted to be moved, since they are fit for children

paragraphs: Siddur hashshulchan letzorek hallayla lo yaaseh ella achar chasheka deen shabbat mekin yom tob, ak kevan sheabar ben hashshemashot shehu achar qeriat ha"mogerab" beshiba daqqim, muttar lehakin letzorek hallayla, vetzarik kol adam lishon beyom shabbat zo achar seudat shacharit kede sheyyukal lihyot neor heteb ballayla, vehu haddin hannashim vehaqqetannim yizzaharu bekak, veachar sheyyaqitz mishshenato bayyom yaasoq battora hannotenet chayyim leoseha vetob lilmod mishna pesachim:

clarification.explanation: The setting of the table for the night is not done until after dark, since Shabbat does not prepare for Yom Tov; but once twilight has passed (seven minutes after the call to Maghreb), it is permitted to prepare for the night. Every person - and likewise women and children - must sleep on this Shabbat after the morning meal, in order to stay properly awake at night. After waking, one should occupy himself with Torah, and it is good to study Mishnah Pesachim.
takeaways: Preparations for the Seder night are not made until after dark
One sleeps after the morning meal in order to stay awake for the Seder

paragraphs: Tzarik leareb bepat vetabshil, veshiur happat y"ch drh"m, veshiur hattabshil tisha drh"m, upachot mizzeh eno moil, vehattabshil tob laasoto betzim sheluqim qashim deellu mitqayyemim bimqomot ellu shehem chammim, abal habbasar lo yitqayyem bizman hachom shene lelot ushene yamim deim chal yom tob bachamishi veshishshi tzarik shettishshaer chatikat habbasar b' yamim ushene lelot, dehaynu ad lel shabbat, velaken tob laasot mibbutztzim sheluqim ki ellu yitqayyemu velo yitqalqelu:

clarification.explanation: When Yom Tov falls adjacent to Shabbat, one must make an eiruv tavshilin with bread and a cooked dish: the bread measure is 18 dirhams and the cooked dish 9 dirhams, and less than this does not suffice. It is good to make the cooked dish from hard-boiled eggs, which keep in the heat, since meat will not last two days and two nights in the heat (when Yom Tov falls on Thursday and Friday and the dish must last until Shabbat night).
takeaways: Eiruv tavshilin: 18 dirhams of bread and 9 dirhams of cooked food
It is good to use hard-boiled eggs, which keep in the heat
